features.name: Academic Attainment
features.description: Captures the level of formal academic preparation in computer science or a related technical field that the letter cites.

levels.descriptor: No relevant degree or equivalent preparation is mentioned.
Mentions a bachelor's degree or equivalent.
Mentions a master's degree.
Mentions a doctoral degree.

features.name: Agentic Systems Design
features.description: Captures hands-on experience designing agent-based systems, especially their control boundaries, orchestration, guardrails, and supporting infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No agent-based tooling experience is shown.
The letter mentions agents or autonomous workflows only in general terms.
The letter describes a recognizable agent architecture, typically pairing Python agents with Go services.
The letter shows deliberate control design for agents, such as permissions, auditability, bounded actions, or explicit end-to-end ownership.

features.name: Algorithmic Fluency
features.description: Captures practical command of data structures and algorithms as shown through concrete engineering improvements or problem-solving examples.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic evidence is given.
Makes a generic claim about data structures or algorithms.
Gives a specific example of choosing a better structure or redesigning logic algorithmically.
Gives a strong example showing substantial performance, scalability, or tractability improvement from algorithmic skill.

features.name: Applied AI Production Maturity
features.description: Captures whether the letter shows real experience shipping AI or LLM-backed systems in production with attention to reliability, evaluation, or failure modes.

levels.descriptor: No AI evidence.
Only vague, aspirational, or lightly specified AI mention.
Shows concrete experience shipping AI or LLM-backed functionality.
Shows concrete production AI work plus explicit evaluation, guardrails, correctness, or failure-mode management.

features.name: Collaboration and Learning Posture
features.description: Captures humility, coachability, and willingness to partner with security specialists or internal users rather than presenting the work as purely solo execution.

levels.descriptor: No collaboration signal appears beyond applying for the role.
Cross-functional work is implied, but the posture toward security specialists is not explicit.
The letter explicitly shows enthusiasm for close collaboration with security engineers or learning from specialist teammates.

features.name: Concrete Evidence and Outcomes
features.description: Captures how concretely the letter substantiates its claims with specific examples, mechanisms, outcomes, or measurable effects rather than broad assertions.

levels.descriptor: Relies mostly on broad claims with little supporting detail.
Names some relevant work but gives limited mechanism or outcome detail.
Provides clear examples of work with enough detail to judge fit.
Provides multiple specific examples tied to mechanisms, tradeoffs, or outcomes.

features.name: Engineering Rigor
features.description: Captures whether the letter emphasizes maintainability, operability, correctness, and long-term care for security-sensitive systems.

levels.descriptor: Shows no explicit maintainability or reliability orientation.
Implies care for quality but not as a recurring theme.
Clearly values maintainable, dependable systems or draws on maintenance experience.
Makes long-term operability a central lens, emphasizing inheritance, quiet resilience, or higher standards for security-critical software.

features.name: Go Depth
features.description: Captures how strongly the letter establishes Go as a central, substantial production language for the applicant.

levels.descriptor: Go is absent or mentioned only incidentally.
Go is mentioned, but not shown as central to recent work.
Go is presented as a major working language in production systems.
Go is presented as the primary or most-used language across meaningful production work.

features.name: Narrative Quality
features.description: Captures whether the letter presents a coherent, memorable, well-shaped narrative or voice rather than a generic checklist of qualifications.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads like disconnected bullets, fragments, or stacked claims.
The letter has some structure, but transitions or the overall arc are uneven.
The letter coherently links background, technical experience, and interest in the role.
The letter presents an especially well-shaped narrative that makes the applicant's trajectory and fit feel natural.

features.name: Offensive Security Practice
features.description: Captures ongoing adversarial or attacker-minded security practice outside routine software-development work, especially through CTFs or similar exercises.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-security practice is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional or casual CTF participation or similar practice.
The letter shows regular CTF participation or sustained offensive practice.
The letter shows strong competitive results or especially serious, ongoing offensive-security practice.

features.name: Open-Source Stewardship
features.description: Captures contribution to, maintenance of, or responsibility for codebases used beyond the applicant's immediate team, including upstream fixes.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution or maintenance is mentioned.
Mentions occasional upstream patches or contributions.
Shows maintenance responsibility for a project or library used by others.
Shows active stewardship of an externally used project, including reviews, releases, roadmap, or a real user community.

features.name: Personal Project Ambition
features.description: Captures the technical ambition, rigor, and relevance of self-directed projects or side work described outside formal employment.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or light side project with modest technical scope.
Describes a substantive side project with meaningful systems or infrastructure work.
Describes an ambitious self-directed systems project tackling distributed correctness, recovery, delivery guarantees, or similarly hard engineering problems.

features.name: Platform Leverage Orientation
features.description: Captures motivation for foundational platform or infrastructure work whose impact compounds across many teams or systems.

levels.descriptor: Does not show any particular interest in foundational or shared systems work.
Mentions scale or impact in passing, but not as a central motivation.
Explicitly values platform or infrastructure work because it benefits many teams.
Persuasively frames central tooling as a multiplier, emphasizing inherited impact or organization-wide capacity gains.

features.name: Production Delivery Scope
features.description: Captures the breadth and depth of real production-software ownership the letter shows through launching, maintaining, testing, and operating shipped systems.

levels.descriptor: Meets the minimum only, with limited tenure and/or only a small number of launched production services.
Shows solid early-career production work, with several years of experience and multiple maintained or launched services.
Shows strong mid-career ownership across multiple production services, with sustained testing, maintenance, and launch responsibility.
Shows especially extensive production depth for this role, typically many years plus repeated launches and clear operational ownership.

features.name: Professional Tenure
features.description: Captures the amount of directly relevant professional software-engineering experience the letter claims, especially in years or overall tenure.

levels.descriptor: Roughly meets the minimum bar, with about 2 to 3 years of relevant professional experience.
Shows solid mid-level tenure, with about 4 to 5 years of relevant experience.
Shows more extensive tenure, with about 6 or more years of relevant experience.

features.name: Python Depth
features.description: Captures how concrete, central, and production-grade the applicant's Python experience appears.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or appears only incidentally.
Python is mentioned as a tool or companion language, but depth is unclear.
The letter shows regular production Python use for tooling, automation, prototypes, or services.
Python is portrayed as a major production language with broad, concrete use across services, automation, and agent behavior.

features.name: Role-Specific Fit
features.description: Captures how specifically the letter connects the applicant's motivations and background to this exact role, team, or posting rather than to a generic job search.

levels.descriptor: States interest in the job with little or no explanation of why this team or mission is specifically appealing.
Shows generic interest in security or backend work but gives only broad reasons that could fit many roles.
Gives a clear role-specific reason such as foundational leverage, secure-by-default work, or security impact at scale.
Connects the role-specific reason to the applicant's own experience or values in a persuasive way.
Uses distinctive, well-developed framing that makes the applicant's motivation for this exact role feel unusually thoughtful and credible.

features.name: Security Assessment Practice
features.description: Captures hands-on experience assessing systems for security weaknesses through reviews, threat modeling, attack-surface analysis, or remediation validation.

levels.descriptor: No assessment experience is shown.
Shows only general security interest or vocabulary without direct assessment work.
Shows direct experience performing security reviews or assessments.
Shows direct assessment experience plus method detail, such as threat models, attacker mindset, attack-surface mapping, or remediation verification.

features.name: Security Automation Insight
features.description: Captures understanding of the role's core problem as scaling scarce security work through automation, workflow design, and leverage rather than treating it as generic backend engineering.

levels.descriptor: Does not clearly articulate security automation as a central problem of the role.
Mentions reducing manual toil or automating repetitive work in general terms.
Clearly frames the role as scaling response capacity, expert attention, or organization-wide security effort.
Shows nuanced systems thinking about automation, such as variant analysis, triage strategy, scarce-expert amplification, or vulnerability response as a design problem.

features.name: Security Credentials
features.description: Captures the strength of formal external security credentials or certifications cited as evidence of security knowledge or hands-on skill.

levels.descriptor: No security certification or equivalent external validation is mentioned.
The letter cites a baseline knowledge credential, such as Security+.
The letter cites a stronger hands-on credential, such as OSCP.
The letter cites multiple rigorous certifications or another unusually strong form of external security validation.

features.name: Security Engineering Mindset
features.description: Captures whether the letter articulates a thoughtful, developer-centered philosophy of security engineering focused on secure defaults, helpful tooling, and resilient systems rather than policing alone.

levels.descriptor: No developer-centered security philosophy is visible.
Shows generic interest in improving security but not specifically in making life easier for developers.
Explicitly talks about secure-by-default workflows, reducing friction, or helping teams do the right thing.
Strongly frames security as developer enablement, emphasizing defaults, tools, or guardrails over policing, process, or documents.

features.name: Vulnerability Workflow Automation
features.description: Captures direct experience building tooling that automates vulnerability-report intake, triage, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or related security-response workflows.

levels.descriptor: No vulnerability handling automation is mentioned.
Security automation is mentioned, but the triage workflow itself remains vague.
The letter clearly shows experience automating vulnerability intake, routing, or triage.
The letter describes a high-resolution triage pipeline with elements like classification, deduplication, prioritization, ownership, or clear manual-work reduction.

features.name: Writing Polish
features.description: Captures proofreading quality and sentence-level mechanical polish, including spelling, grammar, and copy-editing care.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors repeatedly interrupt reading or seriously undermine credibility.
Noticeable proofreading problems distract the reader more than once.
Contains some typos, but the letter remains easy to follow.
Mostly clean, with at most a minor slip.
Polished and effectively error-free at a professional standard.

other.name: Other
other.description: Captures idiosyncratic dimensions that do not clearly share a single underlying construct with the recurring criteria above.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution or maintenance is mentioned.
Mentions occasional upstream fixes or corrective patches.
Shows ongoing maintenance of a project or library.
Shows maintenance with evidence of releases, reviews, users, or community responsibility.
